source_text: ἤγουν ἀνεθελήτως ἐκβεβιάσθαι τυχὸν, εἴς γε τὸ ἥκιστα δοκοῦν τῷ πάντων Δεσπότῃ Θεῷ. Ταύτῃτοι καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος ἡμῖν ἐπεφώνει Δαβίδ· «Ἁμαρτίας νεότητός μου καὶ ἀγνοίας μου μὴ μνησθῇς.» Ὡς δὲ ἀγαθὸν ὄντα φύσει, χρηστόν τε καὶ φιλοικτείρμονα καὶ τῆς ἡμετέρας φύσεως οὐκ ἠγνοηκότα τὸ ἄναλκι, μονονουχὶ καὶ καταιτιᾶται σαφῶς ὁ μακάριος Ἰὼβ, μέλλοντά τε καὶ ἀναδυόμενον πρὸς τὸ ἀνεῖναί τισι τὰς ἁμαρτίας. Οὕτω δέ φησι· «Καὶ ἵνα τί οὐκ ἐποιήσω τῆς ἀνομίας μου λήθην, καὶ καθαρισμὸν τῆς ἁμαρτίας μου;» Προσανακεκράγει δὴ οὖν ὁ νόμος, ὡς ἐν Χριστῷ τε καὶ μόνῳ δικαιωθήσονται διὰ πίστεως οἱ ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ἐνισχημένοι. Αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ μόσχου δίκην ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν σφαγιαζόμενος παρὰ τὰς θύρας τῆς ἱερᾶς τε καὶ θείας σκηνῆς, ἵν' ἡμῖν ἀνευρύνῃ τὴν εἰς τὸ εἴσω πάροδον, αὐτὸς ὁ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν αἴρων, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ προφήτου φωνήν. Τουτὶ γὰρ οἶμαι δηλοῦν, τὸ ἐπιτίθεσθαι τὰς χεῖρας τῷ μόσχῳ, αὐτὸς ὁ διὰ τοῦ αἵματος εἰσπεφοιτηκὼς εἰς τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων, καὶ λύτρωσιν ἡμῖν ἁγίαν εὑράμενος, καὶ μιᾷ προσφορᾷ τελειώσας εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς τοὺς ἁγιαζομένους, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ μακαρίου Παύλου φωνήν· αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ ἐν τῷ ῥαντισμῷ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος ἁγιάζων τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν, καὶ τοῦτο πλουσίως. «Βάψει» γὰρ, φησὶν, «ὁ ἱερεὺς τὸν δάκτυλον εἰς τὸ αἷμα, καὶ προσρανεῖ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος ἑπτάκις τῷ δακτύλῳ ἔναντι Κυρίου.»–»Προσεληλύθαμεν» γὰρ, φησὶν, «Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐπουρανίῳ, καὶ Ἐκκλησίᾳ πρωτοτόκων ἀπογεγραμμένων ἐν οὐρανοῖς, καὶ αἵματι ῥαντισμοῦ κρεῖττον λαλοῦντι, παρὰ τὸν Ἄβελ.» Τοῦ μὲν γὰρ Ἄβελ τὸ αἷμα κατεκεκράγει πρὸς Θεὸν, καταδικάζον τοῦ φονευτοῦ, τὸ δὲ τίμιον αἷμα τοῦ πάντων ἡμῶν Σωτῆρος Χριστοῦ, λαλεῖ περὶ ἡμῶν τὰ ἀμείνω πρὸς Θεόν. Ἐκκέχυται γὰρ τῆς ἁπάντων ζωῆς ἀντάλλαγμα. Προσεχεῖτο δὲ τοῦ μόσχου τὸ αἷμα τῇ βάσει τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου· καὶ γάρ ἐστιν ἅγιός τε καὶ ἱερὸς ἀληθῶς ὁ Χριστοῦ θάνατος. Καὶ ἀναφέρεται μὲν τὰ ἐντόσθια, πιμελὴ καὶ νεφροὶ καὶ λοβὸς ὁ τοῦ ἥπατος. Εὐώδη γὰρ πάντα τὰ ἐν Χριστῷ, τά τε ἐξωφανῆ, καὶ τὰ κεκρυμμένα· ὁ Λόγος γὰρ ἦν ἅγιος, καὶ οὐδὲν ἐν αὐτῷ τὸ μὴ καθαρόν. Κατακαίεταί γε μὴν ἔξω τῆς πύλης τὸ δέρμα καὶ τὰ λοιπά· οὐδὲ αὐτὸν ἡμῖν ἀπαράδεκτον τοῦ πάθους τὸν τόπον ἐῶντος τοῦ νόμου. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ πρὸς ἡμᾶς ὁ θεσπέσιος ἔφη Παῦλος· «Ἐξερχώμεθα οὖν ἔξω τῆς πύλης τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν αὐτοῦ φέροντες,» τοῦτ' ἔστι, τὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τε καὶ δι' ἡμᾶς σταυρόν. Καὶ αὐτὸς δέ πού φησιν ὁ Σωτήρ· «Ὃς οὐ λαμβάνει τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθεῖ ὀπίσω μου, οὐκ ἔστι μου ἄξιος.» Ἔοικε δὲ τὸ ἔξω τῆς πύλης ὁ ἱερώτατος Παῦλος, τὸ ἔξω τοῦ κόσμου νοεῖν. Ζωῆς γὰρ ἡμᾶς ἐξίστησι κοσμικῆς τὸ θέλειν ἕπεσθαι τῷ Χριστῷ. Καὶ μαρτυρήσει πάλιν ὁ Παῦλος. Ἔφη γὰρ ὧδε περὶ Χριστοῦ· «Δι' οὗ ἐμοὶ κόσμος ἐσταύρωται, κἀγὼ τῷ κόσμῳ.» Περιπατοῦντες δὲ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς οἱ ἅγιοι, διαβιῶναι σπουδάζουσιν οὐκέτι μὲν ἐπιγείως, ἔχειν δὲ μᾶλλον ἐν οὐρανῷ τὸ πολί
pass_a_gloss: Cyril (continuing): or rather (ἤγουν) perhaps having been forced (ἐκβιάζω, perf.) unwillingly (ἀνεθελήτως) into what seems least good to God the Master (Δεσπότης) of all. Therefore the divine (θεσπέσιος) David called out (ἐπιφωνέω) for/to us: sins of my youth (νεότης) and of my ignorance (ἄγνοια) do not remember (μὴ μνησθῇς) [Ps 24:7 LXX]. As (ὡς) being good (ἀγαθός) by nature, kind (χρηστός), compassion-loving (φιλοικτίρμων), and not ignorant of the weakness (τὸ ἄναλκι) of our nature, blessed Job all but (μονονουχί) clearly accuses (καταιτιάομαι) [Him] of delaying (μέλλω) and drawing back (ἀναδύομαι) from releasing/forgiving (ἀνίημι) sins to some. He says: and why did you not make forgetfulness (λήθη) of my lawlessness (ἀνομία) and cleansing (καθαρισμός) of my sin? [Job 7:21 LXX]. The law then cries out further (προσανακράζω, plpf.) that in Christ and in Him alone those held fast (ἐνίσχομαι) by sins will be justified (δικαιόω) through faith (πίστις). For He is the one slaughtered (σφαγιάζω) for us like a calf (μόσχου δίκην) at the doors of the sacred and divine tent, that He may widen (ἀνευρύνω) for us the passage (πάροδος) to the inside; He the one taking away (αἴρω) our sins, according to the prophet’s voice. This, I think, the laying (ἐπιτίθεσθαι) of hands on the calf shows: He who entered (εἰσφοιτάω, perf.) through the blood into the Holy of Holies and found (εὑρίσκομαι) for us a holy redemption (λύτρωσις), and by one offering (προσφορά) perfected (τελειόω) for ever (εἰς τὸ διηνεκές) those being sanctified (ἁγιάζω), according to blessed Paul’s voice; He is the one sanctifying the Church in the sprinkling (ῥαντισμός) of His own blood, and this richly (πλουσίως). ‘The priest will dip the finger into the blood and sprinkle seven times with the finger before the Lord’ [Lev 4:6]. ‘We have come near (προσέρχομαι) to heavenly Jerusalem and to the Church (ἐκκλησία) of firstborn (πρωτότοκοι) enrolled (ἀπογράφω) in heaven, and to blood of sprinkling speaking better (κρεῖττον λαλοῦντι) than (παρά) Abel’ [Heb 12:22–24]. Abel’s blood cried out (κατακράζω) to God condemning (καταδικάζω) the murderer (φονευτής); the precious (τίμιος) blood of Christ the Savior of us all speaks the better things about us to God; for it has been poured out (ἐκχέω) as exchange/ransom (ἀντάλλαγμα) of the life of all. The calf’s blood was poured at the base of the altar: for Christ’s death is truly holy and sacred. The inward parts (ἐντόσθια) are offered up (ἀναφέρω), fat (πιμελή), kidneys, liver lobe: for all things in Christ are fragrant (εὐώδης), both the outwardly visible (ἐξωφανής) and the hidden (κρύπτω); the Word (Λόγος) was holy, nothing in Him not clean (καθαρός). The skin and the rest are burned outside the gate (πύλη); the law not leaving (ἐάω) even the place (τόπος) of the passion (πάθος) unrevealed/unreceived (ἀπαράδεκτος) for us. Therefore divine Paul said to us: let us go out (ἐξέρχομαι) outside the gate bearing His reproach (ὀνειδισμός) [Heb 13:12–13], that is, the cross (σταυρός) for us and because of us. The Savior says: whoever does not take his cross and follow (ἀκολουθέω) after me is not worthy (ἄξιος) of me [Matt 10:38]. Most holy Paul seems to understand (νοέω) ‘outside the gate’ as ‘outside the world’ (κόσμος). For wishing to follow (ἕπομαι) Christ removes (ἐξίστημι) us from worldly (κοσμικός) life. Paul will witness (μαρτυρέω): through whom the world is crucified (σταυρόω) to me and I to the world [Gal 6:14]. Walking (περιπατέω) on earth, the saints are eager (σπουδάζω) to live (διαβιόω) no longer in earthly fashion (ἐπιγείως) but rather to have their citizenship (πολίτευμα, word split across the column break) in heaven.
pass_b_english: Cyril: …or through being forced, perhaps against our will, into what least pleases God, the Master of all. That is why the divine David also cried out for us: ‘Do not remember the sins of my youth and of my ignorance’ (Psalm 25:7). And since God is good by nature, kind and compassionate, and well aware of the weakness of our nature, the blessed Job all but openly accuses him of delaying and holding back from forgiving people their sins. For he speaks thus: ‘And why did You not grant forgetfulness of my lawlessness and cleansing of my sin?’ (Job 7:21) So the law proclaims aloud as well that in Christ, and in him alone, those held fast by sins will be justified through faith. For he is the one slaughtered for us like a calf at the doors of the sacred and divine tent, to open wide for us the way inside; he himself takes away our sins, as the prophet’s voice says (Isaiah 53:4). For this, I think, is what the laying of hands on the calf signifies. He himself entered the Holy of Holies through blood and obtained a holy redemption for us (Hebrews 9:12), and by one offering he has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified (Hebrews 10:14), as the blessed Paul says. He it is who sanctifies the Church by the sprinkling of his own blood, and does so abundantly. ‘For the priest,’ it says, ‘shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of the blood seven times with his finger before the Lord’ (Leviticus 4:6). ‘For we have come,’ it says, ‘to the heavenly Jerusalem, and to the Church of the firstborn enrolled in heaven, and to the blood of sprinkling that speaks better than Abel’ (Hebrews 12:22–24). Abel’s blood cried out to God (Genesis 4:10), condemning the murderer; but the precious blood of Christ, the Savior of us all, speaks better things to God on our behalf, for it was poured out as the price given in exchange for the life of all. The blood of the calf was poured out at the base of the altar, for the death of Christ is truly holy and sacred. And the inward parts are offered up: the fat, the kidneys and the lobe of the liver. For everything in Christ is fragrant, both what is seen outwardly and what is hidden; for the Word was holy, and there was nothing in him that was not pure. But the skin and the rest are burned outside the gate, for the law does not leave even the place of his passion unmarked for us. That is why the divine Paul said to us: ‘Let us therefore go forth outside the gate, bearing his reproach’ (Hebrews 13:12–13), that is, the cross borne for us and because of us. And the Savior himself says somewhere: ‘Whoever does not take his cross and follow after Me is not worthy of Me’ (Matthew 10:38). The most holy Paul seems to understand ‘outside the gate’ as ‘outside the world’, for the will to follow Christ takes us out of worldly life. Paul will bear witness again, for he said this about Christ: ‘Through whom the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world’ (Galatians 6:14). And though the saints walk on the earth, they strive to live no longer in an earthly way, but rather to have their citizenship in heaven (Philippians 3:20).
